tokyo_bliss_teppan_shimbashi1.notes: [Teppanyaki bistro · Shimbashi–Ginza border] A calm, grown-up 20-seat teppanyaki bistro (8 counter seats, 12 at tables), open since August 2022 and run under a restaurant group. The cooking is done in front of you at the counter. The most popular Bliss Course (¥9,800, 8 dishes) runs through appetizers, Wagyu roast beef, shrimp and mushroom ajillo with baguette, a salad, a Hitachi-beef and Umesato-pork hamburg steak with demi-glace and cheese, an A5 Wagyu steak with rock salt, onion sauce or kabosu pepper, and a black-truffle and Parmigiano risotto-style omelette. Shorter ¥5,800 and ¥7,000 courses finish with garlic rice and boiled squid. A 2-hour free-flow costs ¥4,200 (October 2026). Children are welcome on reserved Saturdays.

tokyo_howlin_ginza6.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog’s listing ticks vegan and vegetarian options and the kitchen stresses vegetables, but no source names a vegan dish; diners mention carrot soup and organic salad alongside eggs, meat and fish.
tokyo_howlin_ginza6.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:00–23:00 (food L.O. 22:00, drinks 22:30); lunch by course reservation only; closed Sundays and holidays (Tabelog). ¥500 cover. Cards, IC and QR accepted.
tokyo_howlin_ginza6.notes: [Italian · Moldovan wine in Ginza 6-chōme] A homey second-floor Italian bar of 22 seats, mostly at the counter, open since 2020. It reopened in May 2026 after the building's renovation. The kitchen builds on carefully sourced ingredients listed on a blackboard: organic eggs from Kuro Fuji Farm, Tosa Akaushi beef, no-till brown rice from Fujisaki Farm and fresh pasta from Awaji Noodle Company. 2026 diners order the fluffy soufflé omelette, carrot soup, organic salad, corn quiche, beef carpaccio, low-temperature roast pork, shrimp ajillo, a spicy curry and Neapolitan pasta. About 25 wines are always open, many from Moldova. Cover ¥500; about ¥5,000–6,000 a head.

chef_bio.philosophy: "Healthy and safe ingredients, served at their best" (blackboard, per a 2026 review).

tokyo_ginza_fujimaru_ginza4.gf_detail: Ask. A set French teppan course built on butter and reduction sauces; recent courses included homemade bread, fried churros, beef en croûte and curry with butter rice. No source mentions a gluten-free version.
tokyo_ginza_fujimaru_ginza4.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a set course of Wagyu, foie gras, abalone, lobster, eel and sea urchin.
tokyo_ginza_fujimaru_ginza4.hours_raw: Daily 12:00–15:00 (last entry 13:00) and 18:00–22:30 (last entry 20:00), reservation only; closed Wednesdays and the 1st and 3rd Tuesdays (Tabelog). 10% service charge. Cards accepted; no e-money or QR.
tokyo_ginza_fujimaru_ginza4.notes: [French teppan · 8 seats] A cave-like, glamorous room with just eight counter seats around a large teppan, open since October 2019. Chef Fujimaru cooks French courses in front of you with the emphasis on sauces, and the menu changes about every two months. A September 2026 course ran Saga-beef prosciutto on churros with summer truffle, charcoal-grilled eel with foie gras and black-truffle sauce, corn mousse with sea urchin and consommé jelly, butter-basted abalone with saffron sauce, and a black-Wagyu tenderloin. Every course ends with a house European-style curry and butter rice (the frozen curry sauce is sold to take home at ¥1,500), dessert and cold-brew coffee from house-roasted beans. Regulars praise the even quality and the menu printed with their name. Reservation only; 10% service charge.

chef_bio.background: Ownership not stated; Tabelog corporate-member listing.
chef_bio.philosophy: French cuisine centred on its sauces (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.specialty: Sauces; house curry with butter rice.

anecdotes.text: "I come here every time the menu changes, which is about every two months… every dish here is truly delicious." — August 2026, 8th visit.

tokyo_caveau_sentir_ginza6.gf_detail: Ask. Seasonal French pairing courses; recent courses included bread, a pâte-sucrée tartlet and a coq au vin. No source mentions gluten-free handling.
tokyo_caveau_sentir_ginza6.vegan_detail: Not vegan: courses of salmon, shamo chicken, quail, foie gras and seafood.
tokyo_caveau_sentir_ginza6.hours_raw: Hours not fixed — reservation only; check the website (Tabelog). The website also shows when Shinya Tasaki is present (2026 review). Prices exclude tax; no service charge. Cards, IC and QR accepted.
tokyo_caveau_sentir_ginza6.notes: [French · wine pairing] A reservation-only basement restaurant that opened in March 2026 in the former Le Jardin des Saveurs space. It is produced by Shinya Tasaki, honorary president of the Japan Sommelier Association, and run by Tasaki's company Santir. Twelve seats: a half-moon counter around the open kitchen and one table of four. Chef Ryota Tochigi previously led the company's Yamanashi-produce restaurant in Nihonbashi. 2026 lunches included quail with foie gras mousse, a seafood soup risotto, Amagi shamo chicken in vin jaune, Fuji no Suke salmon tartare and rillettes, coq au vin and a mirabelle tartlet. Because the wine is imported directly, glasses start at ¥500. A walk-in lunch course costs ¥3,300 and the Tabelog lunch courses ¥6,600–13,200; dinner runs ¥20,000–30,000. Smart-casual dress, and no strong perfume.

chef_bio.chef_name: Ryota Tochigi (chef); produced by sommelier Shinya Tasaki
chef_bio.background: Ryota Tochigi trained at French and Italian restaurants in Tokyo, joined Santir Co., Ltd. in 2014 and was head chef at its Yamanashi-produce restaurant in Nihonbashi before this spring-2026 opening (2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: The name’s "sentir" (to feel): a pleasant experience through space, food, drink and service (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.specialty: Classic French paired with Tasaki-selected wine.

anecdotes.text: "I learned that the wines are directly imported by Santir, managed by Tasaki, without going through a distributor, which allows for such a price." — July 2026, on the ¥500 glasses.

"…joined Mr. Tasaki's company, Santir Co., Ltd., in 2014 and served as the head chef at "Cave de Wine Prefecture Yamanashi," a restaurant and antenna shop in Nihonbashi." — October 2026, on chef Ryota Tochigi.

tokyo_the_winebase_ginza4.notes: [Wine bar · a different country every month] A long, narrow 18-seat wine bar up a steep flight of stairs, 72 m from Ginza Station, open since the last day of 2020. A counter runs down one side, with four tables for two by the window. Each month features a different wine country with local dishes to match. In spring 2026 that was Serbian red and white with hummus, followed by Moldova, and diners have also tried a Chinese wine. Staff explain the local grape varieties. Glasses start at around ¥1,500. A friend-recommended gratin and other dishes round out the food. Open to 3 a.m. on weekdays, which makes it an easy second stop. Not for big groups.

chef_bio.specialty: Monthly featured wine country with local dishes.

anecdotes.text: "They feature a different country each month, and I tried both red and white wines from Serbia." — April 2026.
"This month features Serbian cuisine, and next up is Moldovan." — April 2026.

tokyo_essence_terrace_ginza3.notes: [Bistro bar · terrace in Higashi-Ginza] A cozy, stylish 27-seat ground-floor bar a minute from Higashi-Ginza Station, with counter, sofa seats and an open terrace that people seek out in good weather. The chef is grounded in classic Western cooking, the menu crosses genres and the mains come off a charcoal grill. Weekday lunch is a pasta set with salad and a beef-tendon soup that diners rave about; a September 2026 diner's kimchi cream pasta was spicy and excellent. Dinner courses end with a pasta, such as one topped with a hamburg steak, and a retro pudding, and the kitchen will make a birthday plate. About ¥1,000–2,000 at lunch and ¥6,000–8,000 at dinner.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog: a chef well versed in traditional Western cuisine, unnamed; company website.

anecdotes.text: "I ordered the pasta lunch, and when it arrived, the soup had beef tendon in it, which was incredibly delicious." — September 2026.
"The pasta topped with hamburger steak was hearty and flavorful… I also thoroughly enjoyed the retro pudding for dessert." — September 2026.
